inquiry.tuneIn: What do you think an animal needs from its home to survive? Name one thing.
inquiry.reflect: Knowledgeable people use facts to understand the world. What is one fact from this story you didn't know before?

passage.title: Kip the Koala
passage.text:
Kip lived in a eucalyptus tree beside a river, in one of the last patches of bushland not cleared for farmland nearby. Eucalyptus leaves are mildly toxic to most animals, which meant Kip had very little competition for food.

A storm tore through the bushland overnight, snapping branches and flooding the ground below. Kip gripped his tree with sharp, curved claws built exactly for holding on.

When the storm passed, Kip's friend Wren flew down to check on him. She explained that storms like this were becoming more frequent as more bushland disappeared, leaving fewer safe trees nearby.

Kip realised how much he depended on that one patch of forest — for food, shelter and safety. “If people plant more of these trees,” Wren said, “there will be more koalas like you.”
